quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass if you are in the lane with the broken line. You cannot pass if you are in the lane with the solid line.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in the direction of the arrow.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow after stopping.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means do not turn in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal before you can proceed.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the curb with one of your rear wheels.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Point your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park when parking on a hill. Turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road if there is no curb, so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When parking uphill with no curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:

options.text: Toward the edge of the road.
Away from the edge of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When used on roads, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roads. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
Traffic is moving in both directions.
You are entering a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in both directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is moving in both directions.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may turn if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can proceed if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Get ready to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Give a quick, loud horn blast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give a quick, loud horn blast.
questions.explanation: Use a quick, loud horn blast if a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When one yellow line is solid and one is broken, you may pass only from the side with the broken line. Passing is not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means vehicles:

options.text: In both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. If your lane has a broken yellow line, you may pass. If your lane has a solid yellow line, you may not pass.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle may cross the center line to pass, regardless of direction.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Move all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the road when possible. This keeps traffic flowing and prevents other crashes.

questions.question: To help prevent skidding on wet or icy roads, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear when going down steep hills.
Speed up before curves and slow down when leaving them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: The correct way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane nearest the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane nearest the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, then move toward the center of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane nearest the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb when making a right turn.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads where traffic moves in two directions. A solid yellow line means do not pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio louder.
Pull over and take a short nap in a safe place.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a short nap in a safe place.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue: struggling to keep eyes open, drifting from your lane, or turning up the radio. If you feel tired, find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear into blind spots or are too close for the driver to stop or turn safely.
Have enough room to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths of distance from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear into blind spots or are too close for the driver to stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around large trucks where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where a car is too close for the truck driver to stop or maneuver safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check only the left side mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Check only the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Always look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has enough room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down in front of it.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has enough room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic. If you are parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the vehicle rolls into the curb instead.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you intend to do.

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs warn you of a no passing zone.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, it is hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to see. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: It is very foggy. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to high beam.
Turn your lights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light bounces off moisture in the air and creates glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that you can use in addition to low beams.

questions.question: What does this yield sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let traffic on the main road pass before you merge.
Always come to a complete stop.
Turn on your signal and proceed at normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let traffic on the main road pass before you merge.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must wait for vehicles on the other road to pass before you proceed. You do not need to stop completely if no vehicles are coming, but you should slow down and enter carefully.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Mirrors on each side of your vehicle eliminate blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than regular cars, and other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road direction is changing or the road is getting narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make speed and direction changes slowly and gradually.
Drive the same as you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: When driving on snow or ice, change your speed and direction slowly and gradually. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.
